name: HOLZBERGER, Rowan

headline.note: Holzberger's own parliamentary speeches and candidate biographies support farming/station, mustering, service-station, meat-processing, marketing, construction, insurance and political-staff experience. Most employers, legal entities, dates, hours, leave and transitions remain unpublished. Political staff and elected office are excluded, and none of the private-sector spells has enough full-time boundary evidence for a defensible total. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Tertiary institution in Adelaide not identified
career_spells.evidence_note: A detailed post-election profile says Holzberger attended university in Adelaide as a young man. Institution, course and dates are not identified.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Peter Duncan MP
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech confirms Peter Duncan employment commencing at age19 and ending1996. No calendar start derived from age; hours unknown.
First speech clarifies six months as a labourer after1996 return. Apprenticeship was an ambition, not a completed qualification; exact boundaries and hours unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: The inconsistent role description and missing boundaries prevent counting.

career_spells.evidence_note: Later Hansard names Goat Works without dates, hours or legal entity. Service-station work separated below.
career_spells.counting_note: Unbounded employment cannot contribute to the headline.

career_spells.employer: Sheep and cattle stations around Broken Hill and Wanaaring
career_spells.role: Station hand; lamb marking and mustering
career_spells.evidence_note: First-speech sequence places station work after mining, job-seeking and pub work. Removed inferred1996 start; lamb marking/mustering supported, dates and hours unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Private agricultural employment is supported, but not a countable full-time interval.

career_spells.evidence_note: Holzberger says he entered small business in his late twenties with a contract mustering operation using a motorcycle, utility and working dogs. His age suggests the early 2000s but no dates are encoded because the source supplies none. Legal entity, turnover, hours, continuity and cessation are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Self-employment may count when substantive full-time boundaries are supported; they are not here.

career_spells.employer: Self-operated sales-coaching business, Southport; legal entity unknown
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech identifies sales coaching; clients included retailers and a construction company. Client relationships are not separate payroll jobs. Dates/hours unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: No bounded full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Civil construction company, Beenleigh (entity not identified)
career_spells.role: Director and operational manager; formerly consultant
career_spells.evidence_note: Construction client became managed company/directorship. Move to Beenleigh around2006 does not establish appointment; ownership, legal entity and hours unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: The evidence supports substantial private business experience but not a precise full-time duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: ABC's 2015, 2017 and 2022 candidate profiles say Holzberger had most recently worked in insurance. Employer, title, appointment/cessation, hours and overlap with business and candidacy are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but no duration or full-time status is established.

career_spells.evidence_note: First-person speeches place constituent/electorate work in2018 and describe commencement approximately then. Removed synthetic day-before-election cessation. End, hours and transition to Fentiman unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official parliamentary service begins with the 3 May 2025 federal election.

Fentiman acknowledged as former employer and her May 2025 valedictory names Holzberger among electorate-office staff. Contemporary post-election reporting also describes him as working in Fentiman's office. A November 2021 parliamentary acknowledgement listed Holzberger separately as a campaign volunteer, not among Fentiman's current or former staff, so that campaign record is not treated as evidence that this employment had begun by then. Appointment, cessation, hours and campaign leave remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Excluded category; not added to public/private employment headlines.

career_spells.evidence_note: First speech places pub job after job-seeking and before station work; employer, duties, dates/hours unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

career_spells.role: Petrol service, food preparation and cleaning
career_spells.evidence_note: First speech locates service-station job in Tenterfield after agricultural work; exact dates/hours unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

career_spells.evidence_note: Describes two years after mining job. Not continuous unemployment or employment; roles and hours unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, substantive full-time status and/or leave remain insufficiently evidenced; no headline years calculated.

research_notes: Identify every private employer and legal business entity, especially the Broken Hill fitter/machinist, service-station and Goat Works roles, stations, marketing business, construction company and insurance employer.
Obtain exact dates, hours, leave and transitions for agricultural, mustering, marketing, construction and insurance work; do not derive year boundaries from age or relative phrases.
Resolve dates and employing offices for Peter Duncan, Murray Watt and Shannon Fentiman staff work, including campaign leave and overlaps with the 2015, 2017, 2022 and 2025 candidacies.
ABN 59 023 753 539 is a lead associated with Rowan Holzberger, but its public result does not establish the business name, industry or substantive work and is not used as a career fact.

2026-10-02 follow-up: primary first speech supplies more precise role sequence; removed synthetic dates, separated combined employers and added omitted roles/break context. Searches of candidate profiles, business/employer references and public professional results did not identify legal entities or hours. ABC2015/2017/2022/2025 repeats insurance wording; do not treat republishing as continued employment. Names of constituent companies and commercial clients are not his employers. Follow up mining contractor, Wanaaring pub, Tenterfield service station, sales-coaching and construction legal entities and insurance payroll. No duration totals calculated.

2026-10-03 follow-up: contemporary May 2025 reporting supplies a late observation of employment in Shannon Fentiman's office. Fentiman's November 2021 parliamentary speech separately classifies Holzberger as a 2020 campaign volunteer and omits him from its current/former staff list, so the later staff role is not backdated to that campaign. Searches for the insurance employer, construction company, sales-coaching entity, station and service-station employers found no reliable new identities, hours or boundaries. Next: electorate-office appointment records and archived business/insurance profiles; keep campaign volunteering separate from paid staff work.

2026-10-04 follow-up: insurance, construction, directorship and political-staff searches repeated generic candidate biographies and first-person statements but supplied no employer/legal entity, appointment, hours or transition evidence. A 2026 speech places the Watt staff role at approximately 2018 as already recorded; another construction recollection does not name the firm or prove an employment interval. Revisit on archived company/insurance profiles or electorate-office appointment records.
